title: Why shadows have soft fuzzy edges
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why are the edges of my shadow blurry?
What is the difference between umbra and penumbra?
Why does a shadow get fuzzier as I lift my hand?

explain.say: A shadow from a tiny point of light has a sharp edge. But the Sun or a lampshade is a wide light source, and that makes the edge of a shadow soft.

explain.say: Lift your hand away from the table and the penumbra grows wider, so the shadow gets fuzzier. The same thing happens in eclipses: in the Moon's umbra the Sun is fully hidden, in the penumbra only partly.

faq.a: The umbra is the darkest middle part of a shadow, where the object blocks all of the light from the source. During a solar eclipse, people in the Moon's umbra see a total eclipse.
asks: What is the dark part of a shadow called?

faq.a: The penumbra is the lighter, fuzzy edge of a shadow, where only part of a wide light source is blocked. People in the Moon's penumbra see a partial eclipse.
asks: What is the grey edge of a shadow?

faq.a: A very small light source, like a tiny LED or a distant star-like point, sends light from just one spot, so there is no half-lit zone. Shadows are also sharper when the object is close to the surface.
asks: Why is my shadow sharp sometimes?
How do I make a sharp shadow?

faq.q: Why does a shadow get fuzzier when the object is far from the wall?
faq.a: The further the object is from the surface, the more room there is for light from different parts of the source to sneak past its edge. So the penumbra widens and the edge blurs.
asks: Why does my hand shadow get blurry when I lift it?
Why are tall tree shadows fuzzy at the top?

faq.q: Why are sunlight shadows a little soft?
faq.a: The Sun is not a point: it looks about half a degree wide in the sky. Light from its left and right edges reaches slightly different places, giving every outdoor shadow a thin soft edge.
asks: Why are outdoor shadows blurry at the edges?
Is the Sun a point of light?

facts: The Sun looks about half a degree wide in the sky, about the width of a little fingernail held at arm's length.
During a solar eclipse, people inside the Moon's umbra see a total eclipse and people in its penumbra see a partial one.

quiz.say: You lift your hand from the table towards a big lamp. What happens to its shadow?
quiz.show: Lifting your hand towards a wide lamp makes its shadow…
quiz.why: With more distance between hand and table, light from more parts of the lamp gets past the edge of your hand, so the penumbra widens.

wrong.0: Shadows get sharper when the object moves closer to the surface, not away from it.
wrong.2: The shadow fades and blurs gradually; it does not vanish at once.
